headline: A private reflection tool that can finally carry its body
overview: Inner Quest already generated a formidable Personal OS surface. The hard part was finding a quiet generator defect inside it: six required free-form bodies vanished. This walk drives the repaired executable, sends fictional values data through one of those tools, and finds it again with a separate read.
targetAudience: Operators deciding whether an agent-facing product surface is trustworthy

steps.title: A Personal OS becomes a typed surface
steps.action: Connected with the official MCP SDK and called `tools/list` on the rebuilt Inner Quest stdio server.
steps.description: The rebuilt server completes discovery with **143 tools** across the Personal OS: 73 writes and 70 reads.
steps.screenshotAlt: Terminal showing the Inner Quest MCP server returning 143 valid tools

steps.title: The six silent writes are open again
steps.action: Inspected all six tools whose required free-form bodies had previously been dropped by code generation.
steps.description: All six previously dead write tools now publish open input schemas and build request bodies, so the model can send the fields those endpoints store.
steps.screenshotAlt: Terminal showing six repaired Inner Quest write tools with open input schemas

steps.title: A values check-in crosses the generated boundary
steps.action: Called `inner_quest_create_values_check_in` with fictional values data against the recording fixture.
steps.description: The values check-in call reaches the exact v1 API route with the fictional note intact. This is an observed request, not a claim inferred from generated source.
steps.screenshotAlt: Terminal showing a fictional Inner Quest values check-in reaching the API fixture

steps.title: A separate read finds the exact result
steps.action: Called the read-only values check-in list tool after the write returned.
steps.description: A separate list call finds the exact stored ID and note. That closes the loop from MCP write to API state to MCP read.
steps.screenshotAlt: Terminal showing the Inner Quest write found by an independent read tool

steps.title: Private production data stays behind consent
steps.action: Probed the public Inner Quest MCP endpoint without an OAuth session.
steps.description: The public production endpoint is alive and properly gated, but private-account proof stops at the owner-consent boundary.
steps.screenshotAlt: Terminal showing the Inner Quest production MCP endpoint protected by OAuth

tips: The fixture records only the synthetic request used by this run; it contains no Inner Quest account data.
note: Captured from the local dirty Inner Quest working copy against a recording fixture. The production endpoint check proves OAuth discovery only; the repair is not claimed as deployed.
